correctness.rationale: Strong-next end guard yields n−1 independent-clause positions (¬r_i∨d_i∨d_{i+1}). Consistent literal polarity proves AXps=minimal transversals of available true clause literals and CXps=minimal true-literal clause sets. Every full-hypergraph vertex belongs to a minimal transversal, so the all-available valuation is the strict unique maximizer up to the irrelevant final request. Private clauses give a bijection to binary words avoiding 111 and endpoint 11; a four-state transfer polynomial yields the exact Tribonacci count and size spectrum. Every selected literal requires a distinct private witness clause, proving size extrema; at the all-available valuation there are exactly n−1 distinct CXps. The checker independently compared semantic locks/unlocks for every satisfying trace of n=2,3,4, and exhaustively checked maximizers up to n=8.

value.rationale: A single, constant-size, practically natural request/delivery timing requirement has an exact exponential count of minimal sufficient explanations on its hardest compliant traces, although minimal contrastive interventions remain linearly many. The result gives the exact worst-case count, uniquely characterizes the worst traces, and counts explanations at each cardinality, all of which are directly relevant to output-size limitations and benchmark design for exact temporal-explanation enumeration. The claim is not the already-known Tribonacci sequence itself.
